justification: The assembly package has an unstable dependency cycle with the core model package. Outgoing dependencies from org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model.assembly include strong references to model types: e.g. AssemblyProcessor.attachAssemblyToMembers(PackageManager) imports and uses org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model.PackageManager, MemberSignatureParts, MetaClass and IMetaMember; AbstractAssemblyParser.parseAssembly and other assembly classes reference org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model.LogParseException and MemberSignatureParts. At the same time there are incoming dependencies from model and UI packages back to the assembly package: Compilation stores/returns org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model.assembly.AssemblyMethod (Compilation.setAssembly/getAssembly), AbstractMetaMember.addAssembly(AssemblyMethod) and getCompilationByAddress(AssemblyMethod) create direct model→assembly coupling, and HotSpotLogParser/ViewerAssembly/Viewer use AssemblyProcessor/AssemblyMethod/AssemblyInstruction. This mutual dependency (assembly → model and model → assembly) violates the Stable Dependencies Principle because a core/model component (expected to be more stable) depends on the assembler layer (less stable), creating an unstable dependency architecture smell.

CompilationChooser (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.compilationchooser.CompilationChooser) has outgoing dependencies on org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.main.IMemberSelectedListener (imported and used in the constructor) and on model types (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model.Compilation, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model.IMetaMember). At the same time multiple higher-level UI packages depend on CompilationChooser: e.g. TriView constructs new CompilationChooser(memberSelectionListener) (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.triview.TriView#getAssemblyTitleComponents) and CompileChainStage does the same (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.compilechain.CompileChainStage). That creates a bidirectional dependency between this package and other ui.* packages (ui.main / ui.triview / ui.compilechain). Because CompilationChooser depends on a less-stable UI contract (IMemberSelectedListener in ui.main) while ui.main/other UI packages depend on CompilationChooser, the dependency direction is not from unstable to more stable but mutual/circular. This violates the Stable Dependencies Principle and indicates an Unstable Dependency smell.

com.google.zxing.aztec has multiple outgoing dependencies to more specialized, likely less-stable packages while receiving relatively few incoming dependencies. Evidence: AztecReader imports and depends on com.google.zxing.aztec.detector.Detector and com.google.zxing.aztec.decoder.Decoder; AztecWriter imports and depends on com.google.zxing.aztec.encoder.Encoder and AztecCode; AztecDetectorResult extends com.google.zxing.common.DetectorResult (depends on common). Incoming uses of this package are limited (examples: MultiFormatReader and MultiFormatWriter reference AztecReader/AztecWriter). This creates a dependency direction from a package with small afferent coupling to several more volatile/implementation-specific packages (encoder/decoder/detector), violating the Stable Dependencies Principle and indicating an Unstable Dependency smell.

The report package's outgoing dependencies are to core/stable packages rather than to less-stable layers. For example AbstractReportBuilder imports and depends on IReadOnlyJITDataModel (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model), TreeVisitor (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.treevisitor) and AbstractCompilationVisitable (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.compilation), and Report references IMetaMember (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.model). These target the central model/treevisitor/compilation packages which are foundation/core components with many incoming usages. Conversely, the report package is primarily consumed by higher-level UI and presentation code (incoming dependencies) — e.g. ViewerBytecode, ReportStage, SuggestionRowBean, EliminatedAllocationRowBuilder and various ui.report.* classes all reference org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.report.Report — indicating dependency direction from unstable/upper layers to this package. No evidence was found of the report package depending on less stable packages (i.e., stable packages depending on this unstable one) or of cyclic/contra-directional dependencies that would constitute an Unstable Dependency smell.

The runtime package depends on packages that are likely less stable/more volatile, violating the Stable Dependencies Principle. Outgoing dependencies from org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.process.runtime include: org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.process.compiler (RuntimeKotlin references CompilerKotlin.KOTLIN_EXECUTABLE_JAR), org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.loader (RuntimeKotlin calls ResourceLoader.readManifestFromZip in getClassForTriView), org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.logger (ILogListener), and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.process.AbstractProcess. Incoming dependencies include higher-level managers/users: org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.jvmlang.LanguageManager (creates Runtime* instances) and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.sandbox.Sandbox (uses IRuntime). The key problem is RuntimeKotlin coupling to process.compiler.CompilerKotlin and loader.ResourceLoader (concrete, language-specific/utility code) — e.g. the use of CompilerKotlin.KOTLIN_EXECUTABLE_JAR and ResourceLoader.readManifestFromZip — which makes the runtime package depend on less stable, implementation-specific packages. This is an unstable dependency smell.

StageManager (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.stage.StageManager) is referenced by many other packages (incoming dependencies) such as org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.main.* (NothingMountedStage, MainConfigStage, JITWatchUI, SandboxStage, etc.), indicating it is relatively stable/central. However it has outgoing dependencies on less-stable UI packages and concrete UI classes: it depends on org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.main.ICompilationChangeListener (registerCompilationChangeListener/notifyCompilationChanged), on org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.report.ReportStage (clearChildren uses instanceof ReportStage and casts to ((ReportStage) stage).clear()), and on org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.util.UserInterfaceUtil (addCloseButton). In particular, the direct use and instanceof/cast to ReportStage (a concrete UI stage) and the coupling to the ICompilationChangeListener interface in ui.main create a dependency from a widely-used/stable package to more volatile UI packages. This violates the Stable Dependencies Principle: a stable component (widely depended-on StageManager) depends on less stable UI components, so an Unstable Dependency smell is present.

The history package (com.google.zxing.client.android.history) is depended on by higher-level client code (incoming references from com.google.zxing.client.android.CaptureActivity — uses HistoryManager/HistoryItem — and from supplemental retrievers in com.google.zxing.client.android.result.supplement which call HistoryManager), indicating it is a relatively stable component. However, it has outgoing dependencies to less-stable/application-level packages: HistoryManager imports com.google.zxing.client.android.Intents and com.google.zxing.client.android.PreferencesActivity and refers to com.google.zxing.client.android.result.ResultHandler (e.g. addHistoryItem checks Intents.Scan.SAVE_HISTORY, reads PreferencesActivity keys, and accepts a ResultHandler), and HistoryItemAdapter imports android UI classes and com.google.zxing.client.android.R. This creates a dependency direction from a stable package (history) to less-stable client/application packages, violating the Stable Dependencies Principle and constituting an Unstable Dependency smell.

Outgoing dependencies: ParserChooser and IParserSelectedListener depend on org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.parser.ParserType and JavaFX classes (javafx.beans.*, javafx.collections.*, javafx.scene.control.ComboBox). Incoming dependency: org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.main.JITWatchUI imports and uses ParserChooser and IParserSelectedListener. The parser package (org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.parser) is a core package (contains ParserType, ParserFactory, AbstractLogParser, ILogParser and many parsing/model classes) and appears more stable (widely used, providing core functionality) than the small UI parser chooser. The UI parserchooser package depends on this more stable parser package (and on external JavaFX). Therefore the package does not depend on a less stable component; the Stable Dependencies Principle is not violated.

The top-list package depends on several packages that appear less stable (low afferent coupling) than itself. Evidence: outgoing dependencies from org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.toplist include org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.hotthrow (HotThrowTopListVisitable -> HotThrowFinder), org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.intrinsic (MostUsedIntrinsicsTopListVisitable -> IntrinsicFinder) and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.compilation/ model/ util (multiple visitables). Incoming dependencies to the toplist package are minimal — the main incoming reference is org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.ui.toplist.TopListStage which uses the toplist API. In contrast, org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.hotthrow (HotThrowFinder) and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.intrinsic (IntrinsicFinder) are only referenced by the toplist visitables (i.e., they have very few/no other dependents). That means toplist depends on packages (hotthrow, intrinsic) that have lower stability (fewer incoming dependencies) than toplist itself, violating the Stable Dependencies Principle and indicating an Unstable Dependency smell.

There is a cyclic / bidirectional dependency between org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.process.javap and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.loader, violating the Stable Dependencies Principle. Evidence: org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.loader.BytecodeLoader imports and calls classes from org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.process.javap (BytecodeLoader -> imports org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.process.javap.JavapProcess and org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.process.javap.ReflectionJavap), while org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.process.javap.ReflectionJavap imports/uses org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.loader.DisposableURLClassLoader (ReflectionJavap -> imports org.adoptopenjdk.jitwatch.loader.DisposableURLClassLoader). This mutual incoming/outgoing dependency makes the javap package depend on a package that itself depends on javap, creating an unstable dependency architecture smell.

Unstable dependency detected due to bidirectional / dependent-on-less-stable relationships. Outgoing dependencies from this package include imports to higher-level Android/client code: com.google.zxing.client.android.HttpHelper (used in URIResultInfoRetriever, BookResultInfoRetriever, ProductResultInfoRetriever, TitleRetriever), com.google.zxing.client.android.LocaleManager, android.content.Context and android.widget.TextView resources (R), and com.google.zxing.client.android.history.HistoryManager (SupplementalInfoRetriever and retriever subclasses). The supplement package therefore depends on the concrete Android UI/client packages. Incoming dependencies: com.google.zxing.client.android.CaptureActivity (in com.google.zxing.client.android) calls SupplementalInfoRetriever.maybeInvokeRetrieval(...) (see handleDecodeInternally in CaptureActivity), creating a dependency from client.android -> com.google.zxing.client.android.result.supplement. Because the supplement package depends on com.google.zxing.client.android (less stable, UI/implementation-level) while that package also depends on the supplement package (cycle), the Stable Dependencies Principle is violated (a package depends on less stable, more change-prone packages). Specific code references: imports of HttpHelper and LocaleManager in BookResultInfoRetriever/ProductResultInfoRetriever/URIResultInfoRetriever/TitleRetriever; SupplementalInfoRetriever.maybeInvokeRetrieval invoked by CaptureActivity in handleDecodeInternally. These cross-dependencies indicate an unstable dependency architecture smell.

Concrete evidence: CameraConfigurationManager imports and uses com.google.zxing.client.android.PreferencesActivity and Preference keys (PreferencesActivity.KEY_AUTO_FOCUS, KEY_DISABLE_CONTINUOUS_FOCUS, KEY_DISABLE_EXPOSURE, KEY_DISABLE_METERING, KEY_INVERT_SCAN, KEY_DISABLE_BARCODE_SCENE_MODE, KEY_FRONT_LIGHT_MODE) and calls PreferenceManager.getDefaultSharedPreferences(context); AutoFocusManager and FrontLightMode also reference PreferencesActivity keys; CameraManager and other client.android classes (CaptureActivity, AmbientLightManager, DecodeThread, ViewfinderView, CaptureActivityHandler) import and use classes from this camera package (e.g. CameraManager).
